diagnosis.what_happened: During a /learn episode, the orchestrator improperly delegated learning proposal authoring and rule updating to academic-writer instead of dedicated learning subagents.
diagnosis.behavior_caused_outcome: Delegating continuous learning and rule evolution to generic task workers (academic-writer) rather than dedicated learning subagents (trajectory-analyzer, behavior-analyst, knowledge-curator, skill-evolver, evaluation-agent) violates role separation and causes cognitive drift.
diagnosis.what_should_have_happened: The orchestrator must route all /learn, anti-pattern cataloging, and rule evolution workflows exclusively to the dedicated learning subagent roster specified in LEARNING_MULTI_AGENT_SPEC.md.
diagnosis.rationale_why: Generic agents lack the epistemic boundary constraints, schema awareness, and evaluation isolation required for rigorous self-improvement.

desired_behavior: Invoke exclusively native learning subagents (knowledge-curator, trajectory-analyzer, behavior-analyst, skill-evolver, evaluation-agent, curriculum-builder) whenever /learn or continuous self-improvement is triggered.
generalization: Never delegate learning curation, failure mode diagnosis, or skill evolution to generic task agents; enforce native learning subagent specialization across all projects.

evidence.observed_value: Also you should /learn to invoke subagents that related with learning.
evidence.threshold_value: Zero generic agent delegation for learning workflows
